title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: GAR meritorie lose justice yet keep by benignity; Rom 5
pass_a_gloss: GAR adds: Adam might lose justice meritoriously by sinning and yet keep it by God's benignity—as in the state of grace we meritoriously lose grace, faith, and charity by sinning yet do not actually fall from them, because grace superabounds (Rom. 5:20).
pass_b_english: GAR. Add that it could happen that Adam by sinning lost justice meritoriously, and yet by God's benignity conserved it—just as in the state of Grace, by sinning, we meritoriously lose Grace, faith, charity, and yet do not actually fall from them, because God's grace superabounds, Rom. 5:20.
source_text: GAR. Adde quod fieri poterat, ut Adam peccando amitteret justitiam meritorie, & tamen ex Dei benignitate eam conservaret, quomodo nimirum in statu Gratiae, peccando, meritorie amittimus Gratiam, fidem, charitatem, nec tamen actu ab eis excidimus, quia Dei gratia superabundat, Roman. 5. 20.

choices.choice: Lose justice meritoriously yet keep by benignity; grace analogy Rom 5
